newsitem.title: USA: ITT Industries names Macher unit chief.
newsitem.headline: ITT Industries names Macher unit chief.

text.p: ITT Industries Inc named Frank Macher president of ITT Automotive, based in Auburn Hills, Michigan, and senior vice president of the parent company.
Macher joins the company after a 30-year career at Ford Motor Co, where he most recently served as vice president and general manager of the Automotive Components division.
In that role, he had complete responsibility for a $10 billion production and sales organization, with 48,000 employees working in more than 50 facilities around the world.
ITT Industries said Macher's organization supplied components to Toyota, Honda, Nissan and Renault, as well as the aftermarket.
Macher will now run a company with $5.5 billion in sales and generates about 54 percent of ITT Industries's $610 million in operating income on a 1996 proforma basis, ITT Industries said.
Macher said in a telephone interview that he's been involved in a variety of roles at Ford, including a stint in Japan, which would help him at ITT.

Part of his plans for the company will be to take the company's brake and electrical systems "to the next step," Macher said. Also, Macher said his experience in Japan could help the company's presence in Asia.

ITT Industries chairman and chief executive officer Travis Engen said in a telephone interview that part of ITT's strategy is to incorporate more components into its manufacturing for its customers, as a means to grow revenues.
For example, anti-lock braking systems are now including traction control systems. This expands the company's business and relieves automakers from more work on the assembly line, Engen said.
